text: What is the capital of Ireland? Answer in one sentence.
Define p99 latency in one sentence, for an engineer who runs model servers.
Name three HTTP status codes that mean the client should not retry blindly.
In one sentence, what does TTFT measure on a streaming LLM response?
Is 0.0 a valid temperature for greedy decoding? Reply yes or no and one clause of why it can still fail on some servers.

A Dublin commuter rail service posts this notice: the 07:40 from Maynooth is cancelled; the 07:55 will run 8 cars instead of 4; Pearse station is exit-only until 09:10 because of a fire-panel fault; Connolly remains open; ticket barriers at Drumcondra are on free-exit. A passenger with a bicycle and a connection to the DART at Pearse at 08:20 asks what to do. Summarize the constraints and give one concrete plan. Do not invent extra services.

Incident note: checkout error rate rose from 0.4% to 6% at 14:06 UTC. The only deploy in the window was payments-api 1.18.3, which added a 250ms client timeout on the tax service. Tax p95 was already 400ms. CPU on payments-api was flat. The database showed no new slow queries. Write a short status update that separates what is known from what is still a hypothesis.

Release checklist for a model server: image digest pinned, tokenizer revision recorded, max model length set to 8192, GPU memory utilization 0.90, request timeout 120s, two warmup requests discarded, dashboard scrape interval 15s, on-call channel #inference-pager. A new teammate asks which of these items change the numbers a benchmark would report and which are only operational. Answer in two short lists.

Support transcript: the customer says the chatbot 'got slower after lunch' and that answers became shorter. Their gateway log shows p50 end-to-end latency went from 900ms to 2.4s, output tokens per request fell from 180 to 40, and HTTP 429s started at 13:10. No model change was recorded. Explain three different mechanisms that could produce this pair of symptoms, and the first log or metric you would check for each.

You are handed a benchmark table with columns concurrency, TTFT p50, tokens/s, and error rate. The author averaged TTFT across concurrency 1, 8, and 64 into a single number and dropped rows where error rate was above zero. Explain why that summary can mislead a capacity decision, and state a less lossy way to report the same runs.
Write a Python function `percentile(values, q)` that returns the Hyndman-Fan type 7 percentile. `q` is in [0, 100]. Do not import numpy. Include a one-line docstring.
Show a bug: `def mean(xs):\n    return sum(xs)/len(xs)`. Explain the failure mode and rewrite it so an empty sample raises ValueError.
Write a small asyncio worker pool that runs at most `n` coroutines at once and preserves result order. Use a semaphore. Keep it under 25 lines.

Review this snippet and list defects, do not rewrite the whole file: `timeout = requests.get(url, timeout=None)` inside a retry loop that retries on every Exception, including KeyboardInterrupt, with no backoff, and then parses `resp.json()['token']`.

Write a pytest test that fails if warmup samples are included in a latency list. The function under test is `def stats(rows):` and each row has `phase` and `latency_ms`. Assert the p50 of a fixture where warmup is 1ms and the only measured sample is 50ms.

A closed-loop load generator keeps 4 requests in flight. Each request takes 200ms when run alone. The server has no internal queue. Estimate requests per second at concurrency 4, and say what changes if the server starts queueing so that each request's TTFT grows by 50ms per extra in-flight request. Show the arithmetic.

Two streaming measurements of the same answer: client A records TTFT 80ms and then 20 tokens at 10ms gaps. Client B records TTFT 80ms and one chunk of 20 tokens at 200ms. Both finish at 280ms after start. Compare mean inter-token latency and say which client can support the claim 'decode is 100 tokens/s'.

A summary reports tokens/s = total output tokens / wall time, and also mean per-request decode tokens/s. At concurrency 8 the first number is larger. Explain how that can happen without anyone double-counting, and which number you would use to size a single user's streaming session.

N=10 successful requests. The end-to-end samples in ms are 100, 110, 120, 130, 140, 150, 160, 170, 180, 1000. Compute the type-7 p50 and p95 approximately and explain why you would not sign an SLO off the p99 of this sample.

A benchmark ran 2 warmup requests and 20 measured requests. One measured request timed out. The author reports error rate 0 because 'timeouts are infrastructure, not model errors', and includes the warmup latencies because 'the model was already loaded'. State what you would report instead, and why.
